sentences.text: Researchers analyzed data from patients with aggressive temporal lobe tumors who underwent complete surgical removal to test three specific MRI techniques for predicting post-operative growth direction.

By examining follow-up scans to determine if the tumor expanded sideways, upward, or downward, they found that the diffusion anisotropy method correctly predicted the growth trajectory in approximately 75% of cases, outperforming other imaging methods and showing no added benefit when combined with them.
The authors suggest this imaging approach could assist surgeons in planning operations by indicating the likely path of tumor growth prior to the procedure.
